recipes.name: Apple-Glazed Pork Tenderloin
ingredients_raw: kosher salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a baking dish large enough to hold tenderloin without folding it.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown pork tenderloin on all sides. Remove browned tenderloin to the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle all sides of meat with salt, pepper, and parsley.

Cook and stir onion and apple in the same skillet over medium heat until onion becomes soft, about 5 minutes, and pour in Riesling wine. Scrape all browned flavor bits off the bottom of the skillet and stir to help dissolve them into wine. Bring to a boil and pour onion, apple, and wine mixture over tenderloin.
Mix together apple jelly and balsamic vinegar in a bowl until mixture is smooth and without lumps. Spread jelly mixture all over pork.

Bake pork loin in the preheated oven until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), 30 to 45 minutes. Allow tenderloin to rest for 10 minutes before slicing, and serve each slice with a spoonful of apple-onion mixture.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple-Glazed Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: This apple-glazed pork loin is coated with a sweet and tangy blend of apple jelly and balsamic vinegar and baked with wine-flavored onions and apples.

review.reviewBody: This dish was exceptional! Followed directions precisely, except I doubled apples, and we are not drinkers so I used apple juice instead of wine. Also, I didn't know whether to cover or not, so I covered first half and uncovered last half. An absolute keeper...A++++!!!!

Yum! This dish is so good and so easy. After reading reviews, I opted to increase gala apples to 2 and I used chardonnay in place of riesling (we're not riesling drinkers and I didn't want to have to buy something just to make one dish). I sautéed the pork tenderloins (I used two) in a pan sprayed with nonstick cooking spray in place of olive oil. Once they were browned, I transferred them to a dish sprayed with non-stick cooking spray and added 1 tablespoon of butter to the pan to sauté my onions and apples. I added the jelly, which melted it, and wine and reduced it for 5 minutes to thicken the mixture up a little. At the end, I added the balsamic vinegar. I baked mine about 45 minutes. After letting it rest for about 10 minutes, I sliced it in the baking dish so it would soak up that wonderful sauce. Very delicious! Served with roasted sweet potatoes and steamed broccoli and my family loved it. I will make this again and again. Next time, I'll probably reduce the apple jelly to 1/2 or 2/3 cup. Otherwise, we really enjoyed it.

I just finished eating this today. However instead of the oven I took the sautéed apples, onions and added sherry to my ninja foodi and pressure cooked the seared pork loin for 4 minutes. OMG this was the absolute best pork loin I have ever had. The taste just permeated the meat and so juicy and tender. First time pressure cooking a pork loin and will use this recipe over and over. Awesome recipe.

This was really good! The only changes I made were using Chardonnay instead of Riesling wine and increasing the chopped parsley to 4 tsp instead of 2. That should have been insignificant as far as taste, but 2 tsp was not enough to spread on both sides of the tenderloin. As mentioned in other reviews, I peeled the apples, and I reduced and thickened the sauce on the stove top after removing the cooked apples. I agree with others, too, that less sauce would have been sufficient. The meat was tender, moist and the sauce very tasty. My husband and I had the pork with seasoned broccoli and black eyed peas since it was January 1! This is definitely good enough for company and will be made again.

This was delicious! I used 2 lbs. of meat so used more herbs. Added fennel seed to the herb mixture. The gravy is superb but needs to be doubled or tripled. I shake flour and water in a jar and add to the drippings to achieve the amount I need. No lumps this way.

I've made this three times and my last attempt was the best!! I used two apples diced fairly small. In the apple mix I added three Tbs of apple butter, 1 Tbs chopped garlic and balsamic reduction with 2tsp salted butter let this simmer and thicken them poured it over my pork loin. Baked uncovered and basted x2 for 35 minutes. Perfect!! Moist, juicy and tons of flavor. oh yeah, I added fresh rosemary to the parsley and it went really well with the apples. The first two times I used apple jelly but the Apple butter is a much better flavor. You won't go wrong with this recipe!!!

To make this even easier and faster, use the same oven-proof skillet start to finish and a higher heat. Instead of transferring the cooked onions, apples and reduced liquid to a separate baking dish, just add the tenderloins back into the same oven-proof pan. Spoon the sauce over them and put into 450 degree oven for 15-25 minutes until thermometer reads appropriate temp. Oven length will depend on how long you browned the meat so how cooked they already are. Served over rice.

I doubled the recipe, and put it in the crock pot after browning the pork in the skillet. I also added some minced garlic. After four hours on high, the pork was falling apart tender. The "juice" was both sweet and savory. I had my teenaged grandsons over for the weekend, and everyone loved this dish. I added some rice to the leftovers and we had a second meal.

I have made this recipe twice now in the last two weeks. My first attempt I didn’t have wine and used apple cider vinegar along with grape jelly as that’s what I had. It turned out wonderful! Those were the only changes I made. The second time I used apple juice instead of wine as someone else had suggested. I used raspberry seedless jelly as I couldn’t find apple jelly and I added two minced garlic cloves to the apple, onion, and apple juice mixture. Oh my, now that’s what I am talking about!! Just amazing!! Great main course for entertaining friends. Of course depending on the number of people you may have to double the recipe but......it is absolutely scrumptious!! Thank you for this amazing recipe!! Definitely a keeper!

Made this last night for dinner and it was a hit with the family. It was an easy dish to execute. One cooking step I changed was to salt & pepper the tenderloin before searing. I also used the advice of another to heat the jelly/vinegar mixture to help it blend without lumps. Like others, I used 2 apples & a touch more onion & finally used chardonnay as it's what I had on hand. I served it with steamed asparagus & a baked potato. I'll definitely make it again. I could also see experimenting in making it into a one dish meal by adding carrots & yukon gold potatoes. :)

Followed the directions and a few inputs from other reviews. This was an exceptional dish, especially the left overs. I paired with rice and roasted veggies (squash, zucchini, red potatoes, garlic, pearl onions, and rosemary). The sauce was very runny, so put the juices in a pan with about 1 tbsp of cornstarch. Fantastic meal.
I used a Granny Smith apple and Pinot Grigio wine as that is what I had on hand. Total oven time was about 30 mins, but upped the heat to 400 F on convection for the last 15 mins. Turned out amazing!

When I began to make this tenderloin, my husband asked why I didn’t simply buy a pre-seasoned one. Now he knows why - this was fantastic so tender and just sweet enough! I used 2 small gala apples and next time will add an extra - they were that good! I didn’t have Riesling ( though that would have been good!) so opted for apple juice. I covered it 15 minutes and uncovered 17 and voila- it was perfect! Thank you - will make again! edit 3/15/25: My husband asked me to make this again. I knew I didn’t have apple jelly but thought I had pear. It turned out to be peach jam. I didn’t have enough so scraped my jars of orange marmalade and mango chutney to make 1 cup (but mostly peach). Also I used 2 Granny Smith apples instead of Gala. No complaints - still yummy- very versatile recipe!

Followed the recipe, except used 4 apples per tenderloin. Made tenderloins one at a time. Made with baked asparagus (EVOO, fresh lemon juice & zest, grated garlic topped with fresh grated Parmesan) and parsley mini gold potatoes.
This is my favorite way to cook pork tenderloin. The apples and onions complement the pork, and the apple jelly and balsamic vinegar flavor the meat. Just delicious!
VERY good!!! Next time I'm not browning it in the hot oil cause that was a mess.
I didn't have any apple jelly so I substituted homemade applesauce. Delicious!
Very good! Unique flavors. Not too difficult to make. Used twice as many onions and apples. Also used Chardonnay, but will likely use Riesling next time.

I didn't believe that this recipe could be as good as all the reviews claim, but holy cow (or pig?) this was among the best pork tenderloin recipes ever! I did not have apple jelly on hand so I used Mae ploy sweet chili sauce, because that's all I had as a substitute. oh my this was amazing! The sweet chili sauce added just the right amount of savory and spice to complement the sweetness of the other ingredients. I am definitely keeping this recipe in regular rotation.

A versatile recipe! I used what ingredients were available to me. I could not find apple jam, which I found strange because here in Northern Europe they have a hundred types of jams, jellies and confit. So, I used plum jam. This was delicious and I highly recommend it. Enjoy!
